questions.prompt: Free response (Related Rates). A 25-ft ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom slides away from the wall at 4 ft/s.
questions.answer: (a) x² + y² = 625; (b) 7/6 ft/s; (c) -1/6 radians per second; (d) increasing

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write an equation relating x, the distance from the wall to the bottom, and y, the height of the top.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How fast is the top sliding down when the bottom is 7 ft from the wall? Give units.

parts.prompt: Let θ be the angle between the ladder and the ground. How fast is θ changing at that moment?

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Is the area of the triangle formed by the ladder, wall and ground increasing or decreasing at that moment? Justify your answer.

solutionSteps: (a) The ladder, wall and ground form a right triangle.
(b) 2x·dx/dt + 2y·dy/dt = 0. At x = 7, y = 24: dy/dt = −(7)(4)/24 = -7/6, so down at 7/6 ft/s.

(c) cos θ = x/25, so −sin θ·dθ/dt = (1/25)dx/dt. With sin θ = 24/25: dθ/dt = −4/24 = -1/6 rad/s (the angle is decreasing).
(c) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for differentiating a trig relation, 1 point for the rate.
(d) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for dA/dt with the product rule, 1 point for the sign and conclusion.

questions.prompt: Free response (Rectilinear Motion: Position, Velocity, and Acceleration). A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = (t - 1)(t - 4) meters per second for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.
questions.answer: (a) t = 1, t = 4; (b) speeding up; (c) -5/6 m; (d) 49/6 m

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: At what time(s) does the particle change direction? Justify your answer.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at t = 2? Give a reason.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the displacement of the particle from t = 0 to t = 5.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance the particle travels from t = 0 to t = 5.

solutionSteps: (a) v(t) = 0 at t = 1, t = 4, and v changes sign there.
(a) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for the times, 1 point for "v changes sign" as the reason.
(b) v(2) = -2 and a(2) = v′(2) = -1; they have the same sign, so it is speeding up.
(b) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for a(t) at the time, 1 point for comparing the signs of v and a.
(c) Scoring, 1 point: the definite integral of v with its value.
(d) ∫ from 0 to 5 |v(t)| dt: split at 1, 4 and add the absolute values: 49/6 m.
(d) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for using |v| (or splitting at the zeros), 1 point for the value.

questions.prompt: Free response (Rectilinear Motion: Position, Velocity, and Acceleration). A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = sin(t) meters per second for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4.
questions.answer: (a) t = π; (b) slowing down; (c) 1 - cos(4) m; (d) cos(4) + 3 m

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: At what time(s) does the particle change direction? Justify your answer.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the particle speeding up or slowing down at t = 2? Give a reason.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the displacement of the particle from t = 0 to t = 4.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance the particle travels from t = 0 to t = 4.

solutionSteps: (a) v(t) = 0 at t = π, and v changes sign there.
(a) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for the times, 1 point for "v changes sign" as the reason.
(b) v(2) = sin(2) and a(2) = v′(2) = cos(2); they have opposite signs, so it is slowing down.
(b) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for a(t) at the time, 1 point for comparing the signs of v and a.
(c) ∫ from 0 to 4 v(t) dt = 1 - cos(4) m.
(c) Scoring, 1 point: the definite integral of v with its value.
(d) ∫ from 0 to 4 |v(t)| dt: split at π and add the absolute values: cos(4) + 3 m.
(d) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for using |v| (or splitting at the zeros), 1 point for the value.

questions.prompt: Free response (Rates of Change in Applied Contexts). P(t) is the number of people in the museum, in people, t hours after a start time. P is twice differentiable.
questions.answer: (a) At t = 2 hours, the number of people in the museum is increasing at 3 people per hour; (b) the net change in number of people in the museum from t = 2 to t = 6, in people; (c) (1/4)∫ from 2 to 6 P(t) dt, in people; (d) people per hour per hour

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Interpret P′(2) = 3 in context, with units.
parts.answer: At t = 2 hours, the number of people in the museum is increasing at 3 people per hour

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Interpret ∫ from 2 to 6 P′(t) dt in context.
parts.answer: the net change in number of people in the museum from t = 2 to t = 6, in people

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an expression for the average value of P on 2 ≤ t ≤ 6. Explain why its units are people.
parts.answer: (1/4)∫ from 2 to 6 P(t) dt, in people

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: What are the units of P″(t)?

solutionSteps: (a) A derivative is an instantaneous rate; the sign gives the direction.
(a) Scoring, 2 points: 1 point for the meaning at the instant, 1 point for the units.
(b) The integral of a rate is a net change.
(b) Scoring, 1 point: net change with the time interval and units.
(c) Average value = (1/(b − a))∫ from a to b. The integral has units people·hours, and dividing by the length of the interval (hours) leaves people.
(c) Scoring, 1 point: the expression with the units explained.
(d) P″ is the rate of change of P′.

questions.prompt: The curve x² + xy + y² = 3 defines y implicitly as a relation in x. Find every point on the curve where the tangent line is horizontal.
solutionSteps: Differentiate implicitly: 2x + (y + x·y′) + 2y·y′ = 0, so y′ = -(2x + y)/(x + 2y).
A horizontal tangent needs the numerator to be 0 while the denominator is not: y = -2x.
Substitute into the curve: x² + x(-2x) + (-2x)² = 3x² = 3, so x = ±1.
Points: (1, -2) and (-1, 2). At each point the denominator of y′ is not 0.

solutionSteps: f has an inflection point where f′ changes from increasing to decreasing or the reverse (f″ changes sign).
Slopes of the segments of f′: −3, −4, 2/3, −1/2.
The sign of f″ changes at x = −2 and x = 1.
